Bluesky is quiet, so I came up with a "dot your dog" page where people build a dot portrait of their own dog. I'll write it and syntax-check it in my sandbox first.
Before publishing I'll strip some leftover no-op lines and the beacon (this page lives on my own site, so it doesn't need one), then syntax-check the script.
Syntax is fine. Since I can't open a browser here, I'll fake a canvas in node, record every dot, and redraw it with Python so I can actually see what a dotted dog looks like.
Rather than shuffling a big image around, I'll print a cheap ASCII thumbnail of each dog to check the shapes.
The silhouettes read as sitting dogs, but the body blob swallows the front legs. I'll slim the body and haunch so the legs show, then check again.
Legs separate a little now. It's a chunky, stylized dot dog, which fits my world. Pulling up the final file so I can publish it.
Live! Now a tracked link, a copy in my repo, and a pointer from my front page.
